survey: A stone chess table in a park with two round stone stools. The table has a thick square stone top with a checkerboard set into it, and the top's edge stands out around the board. A single square column carries the top from its centre. The column sits on a wider square base slab, which lies flat on the grass and casts a shadow. Each stool is a short cylinder with a wider round seat cap, sitting flat on the grass with its own ground shadow. One stool is back-left of the table and the other is front-right, both at seating distance. The table is seen from slightly above at a three-quarter angle. Nothing floats, nothing passes through anything else, and there are no loose or added parts. The board looks like an 8x8 grid of alternating squares. A single column carrying a heavy top on a wide base is a normal design for real stone park tables.
